719.1: Raag Bairari, Ghar 1, Dupade, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. O mind, listen to the story of the Indescribable, the Name of the Lord; riddhis, wisdom, siddhis and peace you will gain: through the Guru's teaching, adore the Lord, Ram, Ram. The many legends, the Puranas and the six schools of philosophy sing the sublime praise of Ram; Shiva and the thirty-three crore (gods) have meditated on him, yet have not known the Lord's secret. Gods and men, ganas and gandharvas sing his praise; all that he has brought forth sings of him. O Nanak, those on whom the Lord has shown grace are the good Sants of the Lord, Ram. ॥2॥
Dupade (du, two; pad, stanza): hymns of two stanzas.
Riddhis and siddhis: wealth and the miraculous powers of yoga.
Thirty-three crore (330 million): the number of the gods in Puranic tradition. Ganas: the attendants of Shiva; gandharvas: the singers of the gods.
719.2: Raag Bairari, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). O mind, joining the Sants, (I) have sung (the Lord's) praise; the jewel of the Lord, Har Har, the Lord's excellent jewel: this gift the Guru, the True Guru, has had given (to me). To that servant (of the Lord) I offer mind, body and all, who has recited the Name of the Lord, Har Har, to me; wealth, Maya and possessions I offer to the one who has brought me to meet the Lord, my Friend. The Lord of the world showed a little grace, for an instant; then (I) meditated on the Lord's praise, Har Har Har. The Lord, the Master, has met servant Nanak, and has dispelled the pain, the disease of Haumai (ego). ॥2॥
719.3: Raag Bairari, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). The Lord's servant sings the glories of the Name of Ram; should anyone slander the Lord's servant, he does not lose his own good nature. All that is done, the Master does himself; the Lord himself carries out every task. The Lord, the Master, himself gives understanding; the Lord himself speaks (in all) and makes (all) speak. The Lord himself has spread out the expanse of the five elements, and he himself puts the five qualities into them. O servant Nanak, the Lord himself brings (one) to the True Guru; the Lord himself ends the strife. ॥2॥

The five elements: earth, water, fire, air and ether; the five qualities (dhatu) in them, by the Darpan, are those the senses perceive: taste in water, form in fire, smell in earth, touch in air and sound in ether.
720.1: Raag Bairari, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). O mind, repeat the Name of Ram: (it is) deliverance; it wipes out every sin of countless millions of lives, and the Lord carries (one) across the world-ocean. In the town of the body dwells the Lord, the Master; the Lord is without fear, without enmity, without form. The Lord dwells near, yet nothing of him is seen; through the understanding the Guru gives, the Lord is found. The Lord himself is the merchant, the assayer, the jewel and the diamond; the Lord himself has made this expanse (of the world). O Nanak, the one on whom (the Lord) shows grace buys the Lord's Name; he is the true merchant, the true trader. ॥2॥
720.2: Raag Bairari, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). O mind, repeat (the Name of) the Lord, the Immaculate, the Formless. Ever and ever let us meditate on the Lord, the Giver of peace, who has no end and no near or far shore. In the pit of fire, hanging head down, (the soul) keeps its mind fixed (on the Lord), and the Lord protects (it) within the womb. Serve such a Lord, O my mind; it is the Lord who sets (one) free at the last. Bow to that servant (of the Lord) in whose heart my Lord, Har Har, has come to dwell. By the Lord's grace alone is the repeating of the Lord's Name gained; O Nanak, the Naam (the Name, God's presence remembered) is the support. ॥2॥
720.3: Raag Bairari, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). O mind, repeat the Name of the Lord, Har Har; meditate every day; whatever you wish for, that very fruit you will receive, and no pain will come to touch you again. That is true repetition, that true austerity, that the fast and the worship, through which one comes to love the Lord; apart from love for the Lord, all other love is false; in a single instant it is all forgotten. (O Lord,) you are infinite, full of every power; your worth cannot be told at all. Nanak is in your refuge, O dear Lord; as it pleases you, so set (him) free. ॥2॥
720.4: Raag Bairari, Ghar 1, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Whoever, joining the Sants, has sung the Lord's praise has cast off the pains of millions of births. What he longed for, that he has gained in his mind; (the Guru), in his grace, has had the Lord's Name given (to him). In the Lord's Name are all comforts and glory; through the Guru's grace Nanak has received this understanding. ॥2॥
